parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Both files serve one concern: they are thin Express adapters over application use cases. They follow the same pattern. Each gets its use cases through the constructor (CatalogueUseCases / OrderUseCases). Each turns the request body into a command using the application parsers (parseAddProductCommand / parsePlaceOrderCommand). Each calls `useCases.X.execute(...)` and returns JSON, with status 201 when something is created. Neither controller holds business rules, and they don't duplicate each other's logic.

One minor point: OrderController.list checks the 'status' query parameter inline and builds the error body `{ error: { code: 'INVALID_INPUT', ... } }` by hand. Everywhere else, input parsing goes through the application parsers. This error shape probably also exists in a central error handler, but that handler isn't part of this unit, so I can't confirm a duplication. The check is also an HTTP-specific rule (the parameter may appear at most once), which fits the controller layer. Mixing method and arrow-property handlers (changeStatus is a factory method) is only a style difference. Overall the module is cohesive and uses its abstractions consistently.
